items.title: UV lock upgrade not upgrading anything
items.reason: Maintainers confirmed that dependency constraints prevented upgrades. Unlike astral-sh/uv#21273, its constraints were direct exact pins rather than Pyramid’s transitive upper bound.

items.title: No clear way to upgrade transitive dependency using uv
items.reason: Related discussion of transitive upgrades. Unlike astral-sh/uv#21273, it requested upgrading every transitive dependency of one parent; here a global upgrade is already requested but constrained.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and all pull request states using literal terms for `uv sync --upgrade`, setuptools, Pyramid, `--resolution highest`, and transitive dependencies; conceptual terms for locked versions, indirect upgrades, constraints, upper bounds, and latest-compatible selection; and version/fix-oriented queries. No matching fix PR was found. astral-sh/uv#11784 was ruled out because it omitted an upgrade request, while astral-sh/uv#18178 involved `lowest-direct` resolution.

type_reason: Pyramid 2.1 requires `setuptools<82`, making setuptools 81.0.0 the highest compatible version. Upgrade flags do not override dependency constraints, so no incorrect uv behavior is established.
summary: The closest issues concern constraint-limited upgrades and transitive-upgrade selection. The reported result is explained by Pyramid’s setuptools upper bound, not by uv skipping transitive dependencies.
draft_response:
Pyramid 2.1 declares `setuptools<82`, so setuptools 81.0.0 is the newest version compatible with this dependency graph. `--upgrade` and `--resolution highest` still respect package requirements and therefore cannot select setuptools 83 or newer.

To use a newer setuptools, you’ll need a Pyramid release that relaxes that bound. An override is also possible, but it should only be used after confirming that Pyramid is compatible with the newer setuptools release.
